cards.html:
Chapter 4 · Level 2: Solid CI. A pipeline that only runs tests is a start. A solid CI pipeline also enforces style and types, tests several Python versions, measures coverage, protects main, handles secrets safely, and does all of that quickly and cheaply.

After this level you can:

  • Lint and format with ruff, type-check with mypy, and run both locally with pre-commit hooks.
  • Cache dependencies, use a matrix build and enforce a coverage threshold.
  • Configure branch protection with required checks, and walk a PR end to end.
  • Use secrets and variables correctly, and know what never to commit.
  • Make pipelines faster and cheaper with concurrency, path filters and timeouts.

What you build: A three-job CI workflow (lint → test matrix → model gate) that is required for every merge into a protected main.

Linting finds likely bugs and bad patterns without running the code: unused imports, undefined names, mutable default arguments. Formatting rewrites code into one consistent style, so diffs show logic changes, not whitespace. Type checking verifies that functions are called with the types they declare.

ruff does linting and formatting, and is fast enough to run on every keystroke. mypy is the reference type checker (pyright is a popular alternative, used by VS Code's Pylance). Both are configured in pyproject.toml:

pyproject.toml:

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 79
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "B", "UP", "SIM"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
ignore_missing_imports = true

select enables rule families: E/F (pycodestyle and pyflakes basics), I (sorted imports), B (bugbear: likely bugs), UP (modern syntax) and SIM (simplifications). strict = true makes mypy require type hints everywhere in src/; ignore_missing_imports silences libraries such as scikit-learn that ship without type information.

terminal:

uv run ruff check .          # report problems
uv run ruff check --fix .    # fix what can be fixed automatically
uv run ruff format .         # reformat all files
uv run mypy src              # type-check the package

cards.sub: Worked example: what ruff and mypy actually find
cards.html:
Here is a small, plausible piece of feature-engineering code with four bugs and bad habits hidden in it:

features.py:

import os
import pandas as pd

def add_ratio(df: pd.DataFrame, cols=[]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    for c in cols:
        df[c + "_ratio"] = df[c] / df["credit_amount"]
    return df

def threshold(name: str) -> float:
    if name == "strict":
        return 0.7
    elif name == "default":
        return 0.5

def load(path):
    try:
        return pd.read_csv(path)
    except Exception:
        raise ValueError("cannot read")

With credit-api's configuration, the two tools report (real output):

cards.sub: Worked example: what ruff and mypy actually find
cards.html:
expected output:

$ uv run ruff check --output-format concise features.py
features.py:1:1: I001 [*] Import block is un-sorted or un-formatted
features.py:1:8: F401 [*] `os` imported but unused
features.py:5:38: B006 Do not use mutable data structures for argument
  defaults
features.py:22:9: B904 Within an `except` clause, raise exceptions with
  `raise ... from err` or `raise ... from None` ...
Found 4 errors.
[*] 2 fixable with `--fix` (1 unsafe fix available with `--fix
  --unsafe-fixes`).

$ uv run mypy --strict features.py
features.py:5: error: Function is missing a type annotation for one or
  more parameters  [no-untyped-def]
features.py:11: error: Missing return statement  [return]
features.py:18: error: Function is missing a type annotation
  [no-untyped-def]
Found 3 errors in 1 file (checked 1 source file)

cards.sub: Worked example: what ruff and mypy actually find
cards.html:
Two of these are real bugs, not style:

  • B006, mutable default. cols=[] creates one list when the function is defined, shared by every call. Append to it once and every later call sees the change. Use cols: list[str] | None = None.
  • mypy [return]. threshold("lenient") falls off the end and returns None. Somewhere later, proba >= None raises a

TypeError in production. Note that ruff did not catch this one and mypy did not catch the mutable default: the tools complement each other.

  • B904 is about debugging: without from err the original exception (which file? which line of the CSV?) is hidden from the traceback.

cards.sub: Worked example: what ruff and mypy actually find
cards.html:
[*] marks automatic fixes; "unsafe" fixes might change behaviour, so ruff only applies them with --unsafe-fixes. To silence one finding on purpose, add # noqa: B006 on the line, with a comment why. To switch a rule off for a folder, use [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores] (for example, allow assert in tests/).

What if… I turn on ruff in an old project and get 2,000 errors?

What happens: Nobody can merge anything until all are fixed, and a PR that fixes 2,000 lines cannot be reviewed.

cards.sub: Worked example: what ruff and mypy actually find
cards.html:
What you do: Introduce tools in steps, each in its own PR:

  1. Format first, in one commit that changes nothing else (ruff format .). Add its SHA to a file .git-blame-ignore-revs; GitHub and git blame --ignore-revs-file then skip it, so blame still shows who wrote each line.
  2. Enable only rules that catch bugs (F, B), fix them, then add more rule families later.
  3. For the rest, ruff check --add-noqa writes a # noqa comment on every current violation. New code must be clean; the old violations are visible and can be removed over time.
  4. For mypy, start without strict and enable it per module:

[[tool.mypy.overrides]] with module = "credit_api.gate" and strict = true.

Concept: Why types matter in ML code

cards.sub: Worked example: what ruff and mypy actually find
cards.html: Most production bugs in ML services are not in the model but in the glue: a function that returns None on one path, a str where a float was expected. mypy finds these before a user does. In credit_api.promote it found exactly that: run_id may be None, which would have crashed the weekly retraining job at 03:00.

cards.sub: pre-commit: the same checks before every commit
cards.html:
CI tells you about a problem after you pushed. pre-commit runs the checks before the commit is even created, so they are cheap to fix:

.pre-commit-config.yaml:

# Install once with:  uv run pre-commit install
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v6.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-added-large-files
        args: ["--maxkb=1000"]
      - id: detect-private-key
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.17.4
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-mypy
    rev: v2.4.1
    hooks:
      - id: mypy
        files: ^src/
        additional_dependencies: [pydantic, pandas-stubs]

cards.sub: pre-commit: the same checks before every commit
cards.html:
terminal:

uv run pre-commit install         # once per clone: adds a git hook
uv run pre-commit run --all-files # run every hook on every file

From now on, git commit runs the hooks on the staged files. If a hook fails or changes a file (e.g. the formatter), the commit is stopped; you git add the fixed files and commit again. detect-private-key (line 10) blocks the classic accident of committing an SSH or TLS key.

What if… a hook changes my files and the commit is refused?

What happens: git commit prints something like ruff format.......Failed, - hook id: ruff-format, - files were modified by this hook, and no commit is created.

cards.sub: pre-commit: the same checks before every commit
cards.html:
Why: The formatter fixed your files after you staged them, so the staged version is still unformatted. pre-commit refuses to commit something different from what is now on disk.

What you do: This is the intended workflow, not an error: look at the changes (git diff), git add them, and commit again. If a hook fails without changing anything (mypy, detect-private-key), read its message and fix the code. SKIP=mypy git commit … skips one hook in an emergency; CI still runs it.

Watch out: pre-commit does not replace CI

cards.sub: pre-commit: the same checks before every commit
cards.html: Hooks can be skipped (git commit --no-verify) and only run on machines where someone installed them. CI is the enforcement; pre-commit is the convenience. Run the same tools with the same versions in both places, or you will see "passes locally, fails in CI" confusion.

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html:
Caching. Every job starts on a fresh VM, so dependencies would be downloaded every time. setup-uv with enable-cache: true stores uv's package cache keyed on uv.lock and restores it in later runs. When the lock file changes, the key changes and the cache is rebuilt. For other things there is the general actions/cache@v6, which you will use in Level 4 to cache an embedding model.

Matrix builds. A library or service should be tested on every Python version it claims to support. A matrix runs the same job once per combination of values:

matrix (excerpt from ci.yml):

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html:
test:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false           # let all versions finish
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.12", "3.13"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

Concept: How the cache really works

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html: A cache entry has a key (setup-uv builds it from the OS, the Python version and a hash of uv.lock). On restore, an exact key match is a hit; otherwise a restore key prefix may give a partial hit (an older cache, still useful). Caches are immutable: an existing key is never overwritten, so a new cache is only saved when the key changes. And caches are scoped by branch: a PR can read caches created on main, but main never reads a PR's cache, and two PRs cannot see each other's. That is why the first run of every new branch is fast only if main has a warm cache. Each repository gets 10 GB; the least recently used entries are evicted.

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html:
What if… CI keeps using an old, broken dependency from the cache?

What happens: You fixed a dependency, but CI behaves as if the old one is installed.

Why: Usually it isn't the cache. With uv sync --locked, the environment is built from uv.lock, and the cache only stores downloaded files. If the lock file did not change, you did not change the dependency. A hand-written actions/cache step with a key that does not include the right file hash (say, a key of just deps-${{ runner.os }}) really can restore a stale folder forever.

What you do: Put the hash of every input into the key (hashFiles('uv.lock')). To throw caches away: Actions → Caches in the UI, or gh cache delete --all.

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html:
${{ … }} is an expression: GitHub replaces it before the step runs. The matrix can have several dimensions (os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest] × versions = four jobs). fail-fast: false is useful because you want to know which versions fail, not only that one did.

Coverage measures which lines your tests executed. pytest-cov adds it to pytest; fail_under = 80 in pyproject.toml makes the run fail when coverage drops below 80 %:

terminal:

uv run pytest --cov --cov-report=term --cov-report=xml

expected output:

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html:
Name                           Stmts   Miss  Cover   Missing
src/credit_api/app.py             33      1    97%   43
src/credit_api/train.py           47     22    53%   54-60, 71-86, 90
...
TOTAL                            166     25    85%
Required test coverage of 80.0% reached. Total coverage: 84.94%

The Missing column tells you exactly which lines no test touches. The XML report is uploaded as an artefact (actions/upload-artifact) so you can download it from the run page, or feed it to a service such as Codecov that comments coverage changes on each PR.

What if… my PR is well tested, but total coverage fails?

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html:
What happens: You add a 60-line training utility with three tests, and the build fails with FAIL Required test coverage of 80.0% not reached. Total coverage: 79.40%.

Why: The floor applies to the whole project. Your new file is, say, 70 % covered and pulls the average below the line, although your PR is better tested than parts of the old code.

cards.s: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage
cards.html:
What you do: Look at Missing for your file and test the important branches, not every line. Exclude code that cannot run in unit tests explicitly (omit in pyproject.toml, as we do for the MLflow scripts, or # pragma: no cover on a single block) and say why in the PR. In larger teams, diff coverage (tools: diff-cover, Codecov's patch coverage) asks "are the lines this PR changed covered?", which is the fairer question.

Interview tip

"Coverage is a smoke detector, not a goal. I enforce a floor so it cannot silently drop, but I care more about whether the risky code, data handling, the API contract and the gate logic, is tested."

Here is the workflow the repository uses from now on. The model-gate job is explained in Level 4; until then you can delete lines 53–73 and remove model-gate from the needs: list in line 78.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore: ["**.md", "docs/**"]

# Cancel an older run of the same PR when a new commit arrives
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - run: uv run ruff check .
      - run: uv run ruff format --check .
      - run: uv run mypy src

  test:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.12", "3.13"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - name: Run tests with coverage
        run: uv run pytest --cov --cov-report=xml --cov-report=term
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml

  model-gate:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - name: Train on the full data set
        run: uv run python -m credit_api.train
      - name: Quality gate (fails the build if metrics drop)
        run: uv run python -m credit_api.gate metrics/metrics.json
      - name: Show metrics in the run summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "### Model metrics" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '```json' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          cat metrics/metrics.json >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The one check to require in the branch ruleset (see Level 2)
  ci-ok:
    if: always()
    needs: [lint, test, model-gate]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Fail if any dependency failed or was cancelled
        if: >-
          contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') ||
          contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
        run: exit 1

Lines 3–7: run on pushes to main and on PRs, but skip PRs that only change Markdown. Lines 10–12: concurrency (next section). Lines 14–15: the default GITHUB_TOKEN of this workflow may only read the repository (least privilege). Line 20: timeout-minutes kills a hung job after ten minutes instead of the default six hours. Line 32: needs: lint means the test matrix only starts if lint passed: fail fast, save minutes. Lines 75–85: the ci-ok job, which summarises all others into one check; the what-if in the next section explains why it exists.

t: Faster, broader, measured: cache, matrix, coverage

o: a fast linter and formatter for Python

Test on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 in one workflow:
100% coverage proves the code is correct.
quiz.why: Myth. It shows lines ran, not that the assertions are right.
